Biala Podlaska New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Biała Podlaska, Poland

Not demolished. This is the newer of Biała Podlaska's two Jewish cemeteries — a companion record to the town's separately documented Old cemetery elsewhere in this collection — established at the beginning of the 19th century (1803, per one report) about 450 meters north of the market square. Beyond traditional steles, it held several ohels over the graves of local rabbis and other notable figures. German forces destroyed it during WWII, using its tombstones to reinforce streets before carrying out executions on the grounds; in 1946, Holocaust survivors organized the exhumation and reburial of victims from around the town into a mass grave here, known as the 'brotherly grave,' and erected a monument that was destroyed that same year — a troubling sign of continued hostility even in the immediate postwar period — before a second monument, still standing today, replaced it in 1947. Part of the cemetery was lost to a 1988 street expansion, the same year the city fenced the remaining grounds; the cemetery is now almost completely preserved, and three rediscovered matzevot have recently been placed beside the Holocaust memorial.
